subject: Egress packet truncation after private-handoff — Brightpoint STG cutover
messages:
From: Adam Reynolds <adam.reynolds@brightpointhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: STG cutover: large payloads truncated post-handoff

Hi Kimberly,

We completed the staged handoff of Brightpoint STG to the private deployment earlier tonight. Since the handoff, our ingestion team is seeing intermittent failures with large payloads (4–8 KB) to your endpoint — they arrive truncated at the receiving side and cause application-layer errors. Small requests look fine.

Symptoms:
- Successful TCP connect, then server receives truncated TLS payloads (application logs show TLS "bad_record_mac" or premature EOF).
- Reproduces reliably when client sends > 3KB in a single packet.
- No obvious error logs from our side besides retransmits.

We attached a short tcpdump and can provide more traces. Can your team confirm whether this looks like MTU fragmentation, firewall MSS clamp, or something on the NAT path? This is blocking our STG smoke tests.

Thanks,
Adam
Adam Reynolds
SRE Lead — Brightpoint Health
adam.reynolds@brightpointhealth.com

Attachment: brightpoint_tcpdump_20260728.pcap (pcap stub)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Adam Reynolds <adam.reynolds@brightpointhealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: STG cutover: large payloads truncated post-handoff

Thanks Adam — sorry for the disruption. I've opened JIRA-NET-4392 and looped in our private-deploy oncall.

Immediate plan:
- Vanessa and Karthik will run an end-to-end trace and check MTU/fragmentation on the on-prem firewall + NAT path.
- We'll also validate any SG / iptables rules that might be dropping fragments or large segmented packets.
- Please keep the pcap coming; if you can capture a failing client->server flow with link-layer timestamps that helps.

I'll update you within 60 minutes with an interim status.

Kimberly Park
Network Ops Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Adam Reynolds <adam.reynolds@brightpointhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: STG cutover: large payloads truncated post-handoff

On Tue, Jul 28, 2026 at 5:03 PM Adam Reynolds <adam.reynolds@brightpointhealth.com> wrote:
> We completed the staged handoff of Brightpoint STG to the private deployment earlier tonight...

Quick triage notes from our side after running a probe from the edge into Brightpoint STG:
- Traceroute looks normal; no ICMP blackholes.
- We reproduced a truncated TCP payload using curl --data-binary against their endpoint.
- Packet captures show MSS/DF interplay: the client is sending larger segments that require fragmentation; we observed identical packets being dropped when the packet had the "Don't Fragment" bit set and exceeded 1500 bytes. When we forced a smaller MSS from the client side, traffic passed.
- On the path we see a NAT appliance (customer-managed) doing SNAT; its logs show it is not fragment-friendly (it drops fragments or packets with DF=1 that exceed an MTU).
- Security groups on the Redwood side are allowing fragments (we checked iptables and SG config); however, the customer's on-prem edge firewall appears to be enforcing an MSS clamp to 1400 in some flows and dropping packets with DF set.

Attachments: redwood_trace_20260728.txt (contains traceroute + tcpdump extracts)

Immediate ask for Brightpoint:
- Can your team temporarily lower client MSS to 1400 (or enable PMTU blackhole workarounds) while we coordinate a permanent fix?
- If you can share the on-prem edge firewall model and firmware version we can check for known fragment-handling bugs.

Next steps (internal):
- Karthik to propose a temporary SNAT/translation work-around on our NAT egress to avoid generating fragmented packets with DF=1.
- If needed, we can route Brightpoint traffic via the older transit path for a temporary window.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Network Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Adam Reynolds <adam.reynolds@brightpointhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: STG cutover: large payloads truncated post-handoff

Thanks Vanessa — confirmed on my side. I pulled the tcpdump and trace from the egress node. Observations:
- The server-side ACKs arrive but payloads are truncated; the pattern lines up with an MTU/DF drop upstream of their NAT appliance.
- We have a short-term mitigation we can apply immediately from our side: enable MSS-clamp on the egress NAT pair and set tcp_mtu_probing=1 on the egress host (Linux sysctl) to allow PMTU discovery to recover. This will likely let their client flows shed the DF=1 frag problem without any change on Brightpoint for a few hours.

Proposed commands (will apply in a maintenance window we can rollback quickly):
- iptables --table mangle --append FORWARD --protocol tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1400
- sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1

I'll coordinate a 5-minute window and apply these tonight UTC 03:30 — Kim, Vanessa, please ack if that's fine. I'll also post the change in JIRA-NET-4392 and include before/after tcpdumps.

Karthik Iyer
Staff Network Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Adam Reynolds <adam.reynolds@brightpointhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: STG cutover: large payloads truncated post-handoff

Team —

Confirming the mitigation worked. After you applied the MSS clamp and enabled tcp_mtu_probing we reran the ingestion smoke and large payloads completed without truncation. We also validated the app-level TLS errors disappeared.

Next steps on our side: we'll schedule an upgrade of the on-prem edge firewall firmware next week and disable DF-forcing rules that were introduced in a prior hardening change.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — please leave the MSS clamp active until we confirm the firewall upgrade. I'll update JIRA-NET-4392 when we schedule the maintenance.

— Adam
SRE Lead — Brightpoint Health
